source: NCHS Data Brief 408, 'Characteristics of Office-based Physician Visits, 2018' (pub. May 2021)
method: NAMCS 2018; rate published as '153 per 100 children aged 1-17'; infants <1 = 596 per 100
notes: Denominator is ages 1-17 while the model's base case is 3-17, and 1-2-year-olds are heavy utilisers, so 1.53 overstates a 3-17 child. Also overlaps the therapy line (a psychiatrist session is an office-based physician visit). Data is 2018 - eight years old.

method: 90% of children 5-17 attend at least one dental visit per year; band = 0.9 (all attenders go once) to 1.8 (every attender hits the full ADA two-visit recall)
notes: CORRECTED: 1.8 was labelled a 'midpoint' but is 0.90 x exactly 2 - an all-attenders-hit-full-recall CEILING, not a midpoint. Honest band is 0.9-1.8; 1.35 is the band midpoint used here. Applies a 5-17 prevalence to a 3-17 base.

source: NCES, NHES:PFI 2023, report 2024-113 Table A-2 + Appendix C
method: n=19,562 K-12 students; PFI weighted unit response 87.8%, overall unit response 53.3%; item FSFREQ: 'During this school year, how many times has any adult in the household gone to meetings or participated in activities at this child's school?'
notes: The category-error hypothesis was REFUTED - this counts OCCASIONS an adult physically went to the school, not participation categories. BUT: NCES publishes the mean as a rounded INTEGER 6 (true mean 5.5-6.49), so decimals downstream are false precision and this alone moves the two-kid total by +/-2.0. The x2 assumes ZERO sibling sharing; two siblings at one school share back-to-school night, PTO, the school play. Strongly right-skewed (public 6, private 10-11) and NCES publishes no median. Applies only to K-12 enrolled children.

source: NSCH 2023 (12.2% prevalence) x an assumed ~12 sessions/yr
method: NSCH 2023, n=55,162, for the 12.2% prevalence; the '~12 sessions' multiplier has no source of any kind
notes: The session-count multiplier is unsourced. Overlaps the office-physician line. A population average of 1.5 describes no actual family: ~0 for 88% of children and ~12+/yr for the 12.2% in therapy.

method: 50 (98%) of states require a PPE before participation; most state high school athletic associations require it ANNUALLY. The 50% participation share is the collector's declared assumption
notes: 0.50 is a ceiling, not an estimate. State-association PPE mandates apply to school-sanctioned interscholastic sport (largely middle/high school); a 5-year-old in rec soccer triggers no PPE, and most of the 3-17 base is out of scope. The 2015 source is flagged dated.

source: NHANES III (1988-91) prevalence via Proffit, x 9.1 adjustments/yr over 2.07 years
method: 9.1 visits/yr (14.8 months of active treatment over 19.3 months) x a population-weighted 'ever treated' share
notes: CORRECTED from 0.288 to 0.22. The 27.5% 'ever treated' input was a self-described blend of Proffit's race-stratified NHANES III figures (>30% White, 11% Mexican-American, 8% Black); a population-weighted blend on any plausible US youth race distribution lands near 21%, not 27.5% - roughly 30% too high. Prevalence data is 1988-91. Named by its own author as the weakest input in the model.

method: NHAMCS 2019: 'The total ED visit rate for children aged 0-17 decreased from 48 visits per 100 children [2019] to 31 per 100 in 2020'
notes: EXCLUDED FROM EVERY SCHEDULED COUNT - an ED visit is unscheduled by definition and cannot be calendared, watch-listed or captured in advance. Value CORRECTED from the collectors' 0.45 (an undisclosed blend that was sitting inside the line advertised as assumption-free) to the published 0.48. Also steeply age-graded (<1 = 123/100, 1-5 = 63/100, 6-17 lowest), so it overstates a 3-17 child.

source: NHIS 2022 (28.4% prevalence) x a declared 1.4 visits multiplier
notes: EXCLUDED FROM EVERY SCHEDULED COUNT - walk-in care is not a schedulable obligation. Arithmetic is fine; the category is wrong.

source: V2 recomputation over the lines above
method: Sum of the six scheduled lines using the dental ceiling 1.8; ED and urgent care struck
notes: USE ~23/YR FOR A TWO-KID FAMILY, with an honest reporting band of 20-26 once the +/-0.5 rounding on the NCES integer 6 and the sibling-sharing question are propagated. DO NOT QUOTE A DECIMAL. The collectors' 23.4 and 24.9 are not justified to one decimal place.

method: Lower bound of the propagated band
notes: Publish 20-26 as a band, never a point estimate.

method: Upper bound of the propagated band
notes: Publish 20-26 as a band, never a point estimate.

method: Tier A lines only, unscheduled categories struck
notes: CORRECTED from the collectors' 15.96. That figure was NOT assumption-free: it contained the unsourced 0.45 ED input, contained an unscheduled category, and embedded a zero-sibling-sharing assumption. The defensible floor is a RANGE, ~9-15, not a crisp number.

line_item: FLOOR - sourced-only, siblings share one school
source: 1.53 x 2 + 6 (school occasions counted once for the household)
method: Same Tier A lines, but school attendance occasions are shared rather than doubled
notes: The realistic floor when two siblings attend the same school - NHES asks about 'this child's school' and counts occasions any household adult attended, so a shared back-to-school night is reported under each child.
